implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: a closure is the pair (code, environment) where the environment holds exactly the variables of the enclosing scope that the body references. Create one by writing a function inside the scope that owns the values and returning it; the creator's locals then become state nothing outside can name. Choose capture semantics deliberately - capture by value freezes the current contents, capture by reference keeps the binding live so later mutations are visible - and state which one you meant. The whole pattern is one sentence: bind behaviour to its environment at the point where both are in scope.
idiom_name: function value paired with a captured environment
pitfalls: An environment that outlives its frame is a dangling reference; specify the lifetime of the capture explicitly.
Closure over a loop variable in a language that shares it gives every closure the final value.
A closure registered in a global or long-lived list pins its whole environment for the life of the registry.
